name: Swiss International (Josef Müller-Brockmann, Emil Ruder)
move: An exact grid, flush-left grotesque, one photograph or geometric figure set against it with mathematical tension.
palette: black, white and one primary
type: one grotesque, two or three sizes

name: Polish poster school (Henryk Tomaszewski, Jan Lenica, Roman Cieślewicz)
move: One painted or hand-cut image carrying a single surreal metaphor, with hand lettering that belongs to the drawing.
palette: a few muddy or vivid painted colours

name: Constructivism (Alexander Rodchenko, El Lissitzky)
move: Strong diagonals, photomontage and type built like architecture, pointing the eye at one place.
palette: red, black and paper

name: Bauhaus (Herbert Bayer, László Moholy-Nagy)
move: Primary shapes and colours in asymmetric balance, with type set in bars and rules as structure.
palette: red, yellow, blue, black on paper

name: Japanese postwar design (Ikko Tanaka, Yusaku Kamekura, Kazumasa Nagai)
move: Flat geometric figures built out of the subject itself, set in calm, vast colour fields.
palette: two or three flat fields with one bright shape
type: small, precise type set to one side

name: Blue Note covers (Reid Miles)
move: One tinted photograph, with type cropped, stacked and scaled to fill the square like a rhythm.
palette: one tint over black-and-white photography

name: Penguin and Pelican covers (Romek Marber, Germano Facetti)
move: A strict band for type and an image that does one conceptual thing, repeated as a family.
palette: one colour per series plus black and white
type: one sans in a fixed position

name: Saul Bass
move: A cut-paper silhouette, one symbol and jagged movement, telling the story in a single shape.
palette: one hot colour with black

name: Dutch modernism (Wim Crouwel, Total Design, Experimental Jetset)
move: The grid itself becomes the image, and the type is structure, not decoration.
palette: black, white and one signal colour
type: a systematic sans, sometimes drawn on the grid

name: Herb Lubalin typographics
move: Letters that touch, overlap and ligate so the word carries its own meaning.
palette: black on white, or one rich colour
type: a bold display face, tightly kerned

name: Push Pin Studios (Milton Glaser, Seymour Chwast)
move: Warm illustration and revived historical lettering, used with wit.
palette: warm, slightly surprising colour combinations
type: decorative display with a plain text face

name: Psychedelic posters (Wes Wilson, Victor Moscoso)
move: Complementary colours at equal value that vibrate, and lettering stretched to fill a shape.
palette: red against green, blue against orange
type: lettering drawn to fill a contour

name: Memphis and postmodern (Ettore Sottsass, April Greiman)
move: Clashing patterns, layered space and colour used as attitude.
palette: pastel against primary, with black pattern

name: Munich 1972 (Otl Aicher)
move: Pictograms drawn on one grid and a calm, rainbow-free pastel palette across a whole system.
palette: light blue, green, silver, orange

name: Mexico 1968 (Lance Wyman)
move: Lines radiating from a mark until they become an entire visual system.
palette: bold flat colour against black and white
type: a custom display face born from the radiating lines

name: Olivetti (Giovanni Pintori)
move: Abstract, playful machine imagery where colour carries rhythm and numbers become shapes.
palette: bright flat primaries on white

name: Tadanori Yokoo
move: Dense pop collage of sunrays, printed ephemera and personal symbols.
palette: saturated print colours, gold and pink
type: mixed Japanese and Latin type in collage

name: Karel Martens
move: Overprinted geometric shapes where transparent colours mix into new ones.
palette: transparent primaries overprinting

name: Risograph zines
move: Two or three spot inks with grain and misregistration, the honesty of cheap paper.
palette: fluorescent pink, blue and yellow

name: Generative and plotter art (Vera Molnár, Zach Lieberman)
move: One simple rule repeated with small deviations until the variation becomes the subject.
palette: black lines on paper, or two hues and paper

name: Edward Tufte and Otto Neurath
move: Data shown directly and labelled in place, with the answer visible before anything else.
palette: grey with one highlight colour
type: a readable serif or sans, small

name: Diegetic game interfaces (Dead Space, Firewatch)
move: Information lives in the world: on the suit, the map, the radio, not in floating panels.
palette: the world's own palette
